meta.index: BobTV is a desktop TV player for Windows and macOS with channel previews and a shared public channel catalog.
meta.downloads: One column each for Windows, macOS and Android, with CPU choices inside. Native Windows ARM64 packages are available; Surface hardware tests are pending.

disclaimer: Check the availability and permissions of third-party streams before use.

home.headline: Watch TV on Windows and Mac.
home.intro: Browse channels, preview another program without sound, and switch when ready. The public channel catalog is updated in the background.
home.image_alt: BobTV running in simplified mode, with sports playback and a channel list.

sections.label: Playback
sections.title: Preview before switching channels.
sections.text: Click a channel to start a silent preview while your current program keeps playing. Click again when the preview is ready to switch, or double-click to switch directly.
items: Program timeline
View the current program and upcoming schedule next to the selected channel.
Favorites and volume
Add channels to favorites from the menu and adjust volume in the player.
Fullscreen and desktop PiP

The fullscreen header places the channel name on the left, the current and next two programmes in the center, and return/exit actions on the right. PiP stays on top and supports dragging and volume; returning to channels preserves playback.

sections.label: Channel list
sections.title: Channels grouped by country and region.
sections.text: Browse national, regional and international channels, plus radio stations. CCTV-5 and CCTV-5+ remain separate channels.
items: Channel order
CCTV1 to CCTV17 are ordered numerically, followed by 4K, 8K and CGTN.
Categories

Pin countries and regions, or edit categories and subcategories. Type a missing name to create it; public edits sync in the background with the complete hierarchy. Right-click to merge channels and deduplicate routes across categories.
Radio
Audio-only streams are handled as radio; a missing video track is not treated as a playback failure.

sections.label: Shared catalog
sections.title: Public channels sync across Windows and Mac.
sections.text: At startup, BobTV shows the local or bundled catalog, then fetches a verified public catalog in the background.
items: Shared records

Public changes, categories, merges, ratings and retired routes are synchronized. Revisions are checked every minute. Category loading stays local to that category; whole-catalog counts appear in the sync badge.
Offline edits
Changes are saved locally and retried when the connection returns. The channel list shows sync status.
Personal data

Favorites have a private backup protected by the original device fingerprint and a dedicated secret. Only that device can restore them; they never enter the public catalog. Viewing history and private subscriptions remain local.

sections.label: Stream routes
sections.title: Alternative routes when a stream stops.
sections.text: Playback health influences route order. Unavailable routes can also be retired from the channel menu.
items: Separate channels
Channel identities keep similar names such as CCTV-5 and CCTV-5+ distinct.
Playback health
Successful decoding improves a route’s record. Failures and manual skips affect its priority.
Route recovery
BobTV attempts an alternative when playback stops. If it cannot play, it returns to the original route.
sections.note: Availability depends on the stream provider and your network. Some channels may be unavailable.

sections.label: Server connectivity
sections.title: Source discovery and AI run on the server.
sections.text: Clients receive channels, categories and routes from BobTV. Packages, guides, logos and sync resources compare the primary site with the cndrp cache. Video connects directly to its original source. Discovery and AI run on the server.
items: Regional ranking
Routes are ranked using the access region and observed playback feedback. Routes without regional measurements still require validation.
On-demand maintenance
The server handles discovery, refresh and AI classification. Clients check routes only for the selected channel.
Network limits
The cache handles resource uploads and downloads, never video streams. Mainland China throughput and source availability still require local network measurements.

sections.label: Devices
sections.title: Desktop playback and Mac AirPlay.
sections.text: BobTV runs on Windows and macOS. Windows can send audio and video to a compatible Mac AirPlay receiver on the same network.
items: Windows
Use the Setup installer or a portable ZIP package.
Mac
Choose the DMG for Intel or Apple Silicon.
AirPlay
A compatible receiver and a shared local network are required.

sections.label: TABLET
sections.title: The same experience, on a tablet.
sections.text: Android and desktop share the simple cards and modern settings. Compact split views use equal panes and at most three category rows. Cards and guides adapt to the available space, video retains its aspect ratio, and discovery and AI remain server-side.
items: Touch controls and exit
Tap to preview, then switch; long press for channel actions. Android keeps an Exit BobTV control across pages and stops playback and background work when closing.
Room for a complete preview
Each category level occupies one row, with overflow attached to its button. A complete card and guide remain visible; short windows use smaller cards and labels.
Original proportions and updates
Video retains its aspect ratio and tablet buffers stay bounded. Downloads show progress and are checked before Android requests installation confirmation.
sections.note: Android devices, Mainland China throughput and Surface ARM64 hardware still need local tests. The native Windows ARM64 packages passed cross-build and architecture checks.

sections.label: Settings
sections.title: A considered settings workspace.
sections.text: Windows and Mac share redesigned settings. Seven categories organize channels, playback, sync, AI, backups and updates, preserving existing features and preferences.
items: Fits your window
A sidebar on wide windows, horizontal categories and wrapping actions on narrow windows.
Keep unfinished input
Categories load on demand and retain draft forms and scroll positions when you switch.
Public tools and updates
Reviewed sources, playback feedback and diagnostic summaries stay together. Automatic update status has its own entry.

history: v1.1.5 · Original window restoration and category menus

Returning from video fullscreen restores the caller's bounds, maximization or native fullscreen and channel layout. Repairs Windows native-caption overlap, PiP return state and the Mac termination callback. Category popups use larger text and buttons with less empty space. Continuous EPG discovery is scheduled development and is not included in this release.
v1.1.4 · Unified layouts, fullscreen and route-state fixes

All window sizes use the same balanced layout, three category rows and attached More menus. macOS Escape and native fullscreen re-entry are repaired. Selected channels prioritize fresh retirement state; favorites retain every equivalent route. Windows and Android physical acceptance remains pending. Platform updates are mirrored to cndrp.
v1.1.3 · Compact layouts and Android exit

Windows x64 and ARM64 installers and portable packages are now available, joining macOS and Android on 1.1.3. Compact views use equal panes, at most three category rows and attached overflow menus, preserving a complete preview and programme timeline. Android adds an explicit exit control.
v1.1.2 · Category creation, private favorites and update feedback

Create missing countries and subcategories by typing. Favorites back up privately to the original device, and other clients cannot revive retired routes. The sync badge aligns right. Managed Windows updates download inside the app and show installation progress.
v1.1.1 · Resource mirrors, route transfers and window sizing

Adds cndrp resource-node comparison and failure fallback while keeping video direct. Individual routes move between channels with public-catalog sync. Desktop startup and restoration fit the display work area.
v1.1.0 · Native Windows ARM64 packages added
Cross-built on x64 Windows. Choose ARM64 within the Windows download group. App, Dart AOT and DLL architectures were validated; Surface hardware tests remain pending.
v1.1.0 · Android tablets and CPU download groups
Adds Android 7+ APKs, touch menus, aspect-preserving playback and system-confirmed updates. Each OS has one download group with CPU choices.
v1.0.6 · Playing-route count correction
Retains server connectivity, channel merging and fullscreen fixes. The main player reads its own candidate pool, independently of the category being browsed.
v1.0.5 · Server connectivity, channel merging and fullscreen

Moves discovery and AI to the server with HTTPS media access and regional ranking. Adds cross-category channel merging, name selection and deduplicated route sync; fixes category loading feedback. Repairs Windows fullscreen chrome and maximization, retaining the three-programme guide.
v1.0.4 · Redesigned settings
Windows and Mac share redesigned settings. Seven categories organize channels, playback, sync, AI, backups and updates, preserving existing features and preferences.
v1.0.3 · Desktop PiP and fullscreen guide
Windows and Mac gain a floating player and a lightweight text programme guide. Windows updates handle locked helpers and enable launch only after installation verification.
v1.0.2 · Update status
Update checks show progress, connection failures and authorization requirements. Mac packages were published first; Windows improvements are available in 1.0.3.
v1.0.1 · Fullscreen controls
On Windows, moving the mouse to the top reveals window controls. Returning to channels keeps the window in fullscreen.
v1.0.0 · Installers
Windows Setup and macOS drag-and-drop DMG installers. Unified fullscreen return behavior and Unicode component-path fixes.

Video fullscreen restores the original window state; category menus use larger text and buttons. Native Mac return cycles and Windows window-state checks passed. sections.title: Installation
sections.text: Choose the package for your operating system and processor.
items: Windows

Run Setup to choose the installation folder and desktop shortcut. The default folder is BoB\BoBTV under Program Files; administrator approval is required. For the portable ZIP, extract all files and run BobTV.exe. Personal channels and favorites are stored in your user data folder.
macOS

Open the DMG and drag BobTV.app to Applications. For unattended updates, install in a writable Applications folder in your home directory. Do not run the app long-term from the read-only disk image. This release has no Apple Developer ID signature or notarization; macOS may require manual approval to open it.
Updates

BobTV checks at startup, every six hours, and on returning to the foreground. Managed Windows installations download and verify Setup inside BobTV, request administrator approval when you choose Install, then show installation progress. Canceling approval keeps the old app running. Older managed clients need this Setup once. Portable Windows and writable Mac locations update after exit and attempt rollback after three failed starts. Protected Mac locations require manual replacement. Without trusted code signing, Edge warnings on a first browser download may remain.
Android

Install the APK on Android 7 or later. Choose ARM64 first, ARM32 for devices limited to 32-bit apps, or x64 for matching devices/emulators. Video retains its source aspect ratio in portrait and landscape. Updates require Android installation permission and system confirmation.

sections.title: First launch and channel sync
sections.text: BobTV syncs channels and complete category hierarchies from BobTV and compares the primary site with cndrp for resource delivery. Discovery and AI run on the server; video connects directly to its source. Clients check the selected channel on demand.
items: Initial catalog
BobTV shows local or bundled channels first, then fetches the categorized and verified public catalog. Channel counts change as sources are maintained.
Sync status
Pending retry means the network or service is temporarily unavailable. Local changes are saved and retried automatically.
Public and personal

Public categories, ratings, retirements and route transfers sync across devices. Other clients' successful playback cannot restore retired routes. Private favorite backups can only return to the original device; history and private subscriptions remain local.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostic logs
diagnostics.intro: If playback or the app fails, you can submit a diagnostic log manually. The page filters allowed fields before upload.
diagnostics.limit: Choose a .log or .jsonl file, up to 1 MiB and 5,000 entries. A successful upload returns a diagnostic ID.
notes: Only allowed summary fields, including time, event, source and runtime metrics, are sent. Raw exception text, paths and playback URLs are excluded.
Logs are stored privately for 14 days, with no public read endpoint. Automatic summary uploads are off by default and can be enabled in the app.
Channel sync and diagnostic uploads run independently. Keep the time, platform and app version when reporting sync, download or playback errors.
The app reports an app-specific hardware hash to count installed devices. Raw hardware IDs are not sent. Old or offline versions are unobserved; cloned device IDs may be counted together.
